title: Base case omission in recursive calls
description: The student likely selected the 'Incorrect hypothesis string' because they are focusing on the syntax or the data type of the input rather than the structural logic of the recursion. By omitting the base case, the student fails to recognize that a recursive function requires a termination condition to prevent infinite execution. The student's focus on the 'hypothesis string' suggests they are misinterpreting the error as a data validation issue rather than a fundamental flaw in the recursive control flow.
trigger_evidence: Diagnostic quiz attempt on Question q-fitb-1790878685740-0. Selected erroneous hypothesis: Incorrect hypothesis string.

remediation_steps.title: Understanding the Role of the Base Case
remediation_steps.explanation: A recursive function must have at least one base case that returns a value without making further recursive calls. Without this, the function will continue to call itself indefinitely, leading to a stack overflow error.
remediation_steps.verified_quote: Every recursive function must have a base case to terminate the recursion.

remediation_steps.title: Identifying the Termination Condition
remediation_steps.explanation: Analyze the problem to determine the simplest possible input for which the answer is known. This is your base case. Ensure that every recursive path eventually reaches this state.
remediation_steps.verified_quote: The base case is the condition that stops the recursive process.

remediation_steps.title: Verification through Trace Analysis
remediation_steps.explanation: Perform a manual trace of your function with a small input. If the function does not reach a return statement that does not involve a recursive call, your base case is missing or unreachable.
remediation_steps.verified_quote: Always verify that the recursive step moves the input closer to the base case.
remediation_steps.source_ref: Textbook Appendix B: Debugging Recursive Logic

title: random-access-broken-by-zeroing-confusion
description: Student selected: "It violates O(1) random access rules, causing subsequent index lookups to throw runtime exceptions.". This reveals a fundamental misunderstanding of Arrays.
trigger_evidence: Diagnostic quiz attempt on Question q-1790869553983-4. Selected erroneous hypothesis: It violates O(1) random access rules, causing subsequent index lookups to throw runtime exceptions..

remediation_steps.title: Deconstruct the Counter-Example
remediation_steps.explanation: Consider what happens when this assumption is applied to an edge case. The invariant breaks because intermediate states are not preserved.
remediation_steps.verified_quote: A loop invariant must satisfy initialization, maintenance, and termination.

remediation_steps.title: Formal Invariant Formulation
remediation_steps.explanation: Notice that each stack frame allocates independent local registers and return pointers.
remediation_steps.code_example:
def recurse(n):
    if n <= 0: return
    # Each invocation creates an isolated O(1) frame
    recurse(n - 1)
remediation_steps.verified_quote: Activation records are pushed to the execution call stack sequentially.
remediation_steps.source_ref: Computer Systems: A Programmer Perspective, Page 242

remediation_steps.title: Self-Explanation & Invariant Verification
remediation_steps.explanation: Verify that both base conditions and induction hypotheses hold for all N >= 1.
remediation_steps.verified_quote: Inductive step proves truth for N+1 from N.
remediation_steps.source_ref: Discrete Mathematics and Its Applications, Page 315

title: Missing or Non-Terminating Base Case Assumption
description: Believing recursive execution terminates automatically without an explicit return statement or that function calls safely unwind when memory limits are reached.
trigger_evidence: In Quiz #4 (Question 3), selected: "The recursion will safely exit once the local variables go out of scope, even without an if-statement base case."

remediation_steps.title: The Call Stack Architecture
remediation_steps.explanation: Every time a function invokes itself, the operating system allocates a fresh Stack Frame containing local parameters and the return instruction address. Without a base condition, stack frames grow until StackOverflowError.
remediation_steps.verified_quote: CLRS 4th Ed, Page 73: "Without an explicit base case, call stack frames accumulate monotonically until a stack overflow exception halts the runtime."

remediation_steps.title: The Invariant Guard Pattern
remediation_steps.explanation: Always place your base case check at the very first line of your recursive function before doing any work or spawning child calls.
remediation_steps.verified_quote: Lecture 07, Slide 18: "1. Establish Base Case (simplest atomic input where answer is known). 2. Ensure arguments strictly converge towards base case."
